rawCommits.subject: fix(left-menu): restore right-click context menu in LeftMenuTree (#74)
rawCommits.body:
The projects sidebar was migrated from the legacy ListItem-based tree to
LeftMenuTree, but `useExplorerMenus` still resolves the clicked row via
`closest("[data-list-item][id]")`. LeftMenuTree rows render `id={entry.id}`
yet never emit the `data-list-item` marker, so the selector never matches:
`handleContextMenu` (and the F2-rename `handleKeyDown`) bail out early. As a
result, right-click in the projects sidebar (Remove from Project, Rename,
Add Agent, Delete Project) and F2-to-rename silently do nothing.

Add `data-list-item=""` to both LeftMenuTree row buttons — the leaf/agent
rows and the project/section group headers — so the existing selector
matches and the context menu + keyboard rename can resolve the node again.
`agentMeta` already includes archived agents, so this also restores the
delete path for archived agents.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

rawCommits.subject: Add usage signal analytics with billing enrichment (#75)
rawCommits.body:
Adds a pure usage-signal classifier plus server-side emission for completed chat turns, persisted as turn_usage_signal and sent to Mixpanel as agent_turn_classified.

Enriches the signal from z-billing account data with account age, funding buckets, grant usage buckets, lifetime purchased/granted/used cents, and balance fields.

Verified with cargo test -p aura-os-usage-signals; cargo test -p aura-os-server usage_signal; cargo test -p aura-os-server --test chat_events_test bare_agent_chat_route_persists_usage_signal_from_harness_end; cargo test -p aura-os-server mixpanel; npm --prefix interface run test -- src/lib/analytics-contract.test.ts; cargo clippy -p aura-os-usage-signals -- -D warnings; cargo clippy -p aura-os-server --tests -- -D warnings -A clippy::derivable_impls -A clippy::items_after_test_module.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: Add usage signal analytics with billing enrichment (#75)

rawCommits.subject: fix(models): drop unsupported 'minimal' reasoning effort from GPT-5.4 family
rawCommits.body:
GPT-5.4 / -mini / -nano reject reasoning_effort=minimal (their native
set is none/low/medium/high/xhigh), unlike GPT-5.5 which keeps minimal.
The picker offered minimal and gpt-5.4-nano even defaulted to it, so
every nano call 400'd. Add a GPT_5_4_EFFORTS (low/medium/high) set,
apply it to the 5.4 family, and flip nano's default to low. Persisted
'minimal' self-heals via the existing efforts validation.

Adds three Fireworks-hosted chat models alongside their predecessors,
each as a plain (no reasoning-effort) row matching the existing

- Kimi K2.7 Code: accounts/fireworks/models/kimi-k2p7-code, 256K
- GLM 5.2:        accounts/fireworks/models/glm-5p2, 1M

Wires the catalog, legacy-id aliases, display pricing, and the
benchmark-pricing script mirror.

rawCommits.subject: fix(model-picker): stop hover flyouts stacking when the menu scrolls
rawCommits.body:
Scrolling the model list under a stationary pointer surfaced new rows
that each opened their flyout; the single-open coordinator closed the
previous one, but that row's still-attached scroll-reflow listener fired
in the same scroll event and re-opened it, stacking multiple submenus
(reported as overlapping panels in the picker).

Track open/closed intent in a synchronous ref so a stale reflow on an
already-closed flyout bails instead of resurrecting it. The flyout still
repositions live while genuinely open. Adds regression tests for the
single-open invariant and the close-then-scroll race.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: stop hover flyouts stacking when the menu scrolls

rawCommits.subject: fix(stream): stop the stuck-stream watchdog from killing live turns
rawCommits.body:
The client-side watchdog hard-aborted a chat turn (onStop → cancel-turn)
after 60s of wire silence. On long extended-thinking turns the stream can
legitimately go quiet past 60s, so this abandoned turns that were still
alive — and since the upstream completes and bills regardless, the user
was charged for a turn the UI showed as failed.

The destructive 60s abort also pre-empted the graceful recovery path: a
genuine socket drop is caught by the 90s SSE idle reattach
(SSEIdleTimeoutError, recoverable), which re-attaches to the still-running
turn instead of cancelling it.

Move the destructive auto-abort from 60s to a 5-minute absolute safety cap
(FULLY_TIMED_OUT_MS -> ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000). The non-destructive
30s "stuck" pill (Stop / Retry / Report) is unchanged and remains the
"taking longer than usual" affordance; the hard abort now fires only after
genuinely-dead total silence (no heartbeat and no successful reattach).
Not killing a live turn also means the user receives the output they were
billed for.

Adds a regression test pinning that the abort no longer fires at the old
60s mark (only at the cap), and strengthens the partial-image guard to
walk past the new cap so it still proves markStreamProgress resets the
clock.

rendered.title: Stream watchdog softening, model catalog refresh, and sidebar context menus return
rendered.intro: A focused nightly across chat reliability and the model picker: the stream watchdog no longer kills long extended-thinking turns you've already been billed for, the GPT-5.4 family stops 400-ing on an unsupported reasoning tier, and three new Fireworks-hosted models join the catalog. The projects sidebar also gets its right-click menu and F2 rename back, and the server starts emitting billing-enriched usage signals for completed turns.

entries.title: Projects sidebar right-click and F2 rename work again
entries.summary: A missing DOM marker on the migrated LeftMenuTree was silently breaking every context-menu action in the projects sidebar.

items.text: Restored Remove from Project, Rename, Add Agent, Delete Project, and F2-to-rename in the projects sidebar by emitting the `data-list-item` marker that `useExplorerMenus` uses to resolve the clicked row — also re-enabling the delete path for archived agents.

entries.title: Per-turn usage-signal analytics with billing enrichment
entries.summary: The server now classifies completed chat turns and ships an enriched signal to Mixpanel, backed by a new `aura-os-usage-signals` crate.

items.text: Introduced a pure usage-signal classifier (new `aura-os-usage-signals` crate) and wired server-side emission for completed chat turns, persisted as `turn_usage_signal` and sent to Mixpanel as `agent_turn_classified`.

Enriched each signal with z-billing context — account age, funding and grant-usage buckets, lifetime purchased/granted/used cents, and balance — plus per-turn shape (plan mode, council, cross-agent, attachments, project binding source).

entries.title: GPT-5.4 reasoning tiers fixed and three Fireworks models added
entries.summary: The model picker stops offering an effort tier the GPT-5.4 API rejects, and Kimi K2.7 Code, GLM 5.2, and Qwen3.7 Plus join the catalog.

items.text: Removed the unsupported `minimal` reasoning effort from GPT-5.4 / -mini / -nano (their native set is none/low/medium/high/xhigh) and flipped nano's default from `minimal` to `low`, ending the 400s that had broken every nano call; persisted `minimal` self-heals via existing validation.
Added Kimi K2.7 Code (256K), GLM 5.2 (1M), and Qwen3.7 Plus (256K) as Fireworks-hosted chat models, including catalog entries, legacy-id aliases, display pricing, and the benchmark-pricing mirror.

entries.title: Model picker no longer stacks overlapping hover flyouts
entries.summary: Fixed a scroll-vs-coordinator race that let closed model rows resurrect their flyout, producing overlapping panels in the picker.

items.text: Tracked open/closed intent in a synchronous ref so a stale scroll-reflow on an already-closed model row bails instead of re-opening its flyout, while still letting genuinely-open flyouts reposition live; regression tests pin the single-open invariant and the close-then-scroll race.

entries.title: Stuck-stream watchdog stops killing live extended-thinking turns
entries.summary: The destructive 60s client-side auto-abort was cancelling long but still-alive turns that the upstream then billed; the hard cap moves to 5 minutes of truly dead silence.

items.text: Moved the destructive auto-abort from 60s of wire silence to a 5-minute absolute safety cap (`ABSOLUTE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000`), so long extended-thinking turns are no longer cancelled — and no longer billed-but-shown-as-failed — and the 90s SSE idle reattach can recover genuine socket drops first.

Kept the non-destructive 30s "taking longer than usual" pill (Stop / Retry / Report) unchanged, and added a regression test pinning that no auto-abort fires at the old 60s mark — only at the absolute cap.

highlights: Stuck-stream auto-abort softened from 60s to a 5-minute safety cap
Kimi K2.7 Code, GLM 5.2, and Qwen3.7 Plus added

Usage-signal analytics with billing enrichment now emitted per turn
